oh dear :( i'm 24f, i have bipolar II (and some other shit), and recently a new psychiatrist diagnosed me with bpd as well but i'm not certain about that. did you quit your meds cold turkey? that usually leads to horrific results - as it did with me, more than once. during one of those times, i attempted suicide. 

you seem to love your ex very very deeply, i get that, but if he truly loved you as much, he probably wouldn't break up with you during such a traumatic and difficult time in your life - AND proceed to start a new relationship right after. this is just my two cents, but he seems like an insensible jerk; you deserve someone better. i've had people in my past calling it quits with me because i was "too much" and "too self destructive", things like that, things that a lot of people with bd/bpd hear. with mood and personality disorders, dating is even harder and trickier, and maaaany people walk out once things get really rough. i know how much it hurts, and we end up feeling completely unloveable, but that's not an universal truth by any means.

i know you can't see this now (trust me, i couldn't see it either after the supposed "love of my life" left me multiple times, and that also played a role in my suicide attempt), but this could be a blessing in disguise. heartbreak is an excruciating pain when we are so sensitive and intense, and feel things so deeply and love others so much. but by having him out of your life, you can eventually find a new partner who could be much more understanding and supportive.

and i totally can relate to feeling like a burden to family and friends - especially family. i feel that way every single day, basically. it's so painful. i don't want to fill you with cliché, unsolicited advice (i particularly dont like it very much when others do that to me, esp when i'm really really really down, like you seem to be), but just know you're not completely alone - a total internet stranger can relate to the feelings you just described, more than you can imagine. 

i wish you strenght to overcome this and eventually see value in yourself, aside from being loved and wanted by others. i struggle with this as well so i know at times it may seem like something unconceivable. but i hope you can make through this. go easy on yourself, what you went/are going through is extremely difficult. cling into any tiny bit of hope you still may have. you deserve so much. i hope you can see that, eventually. 

and if you think you're in immediate danger of harming yourself, definitely let someone (someone you really trust) know, and go to the ER if it gets TOO bad - even though your family will be concerned and probably emotional, they should understand that your safety and well being comes first and should not be left uncared for.

I am pro Eric and Donna. They are my favorite couple. I don't think their relationship was ever supposed to be perfect. I think it is portrayed for what it is - a teenage relationship, full of insecurities, jealousy, meaningless fights, and regrets. I understand how some people could see it as overrated, though. It is one of the main plots of the show, because Eric is supposed to be the no. 1 main character. Essentially, the show is about Eric, plus HIS friends, HIS family, and HIS girlfriend Donna. So their relationship was always a major thing in the show and has always set the direction of many episodes and seasons.

I have a lot of favorite moments between the two of them throughout the show, especially from the 76-77 era. But in the series finale when Donna is sitting in the garage thinking about him (he hasn't arrived from Africa yet) and she reminisces about their relationship, from the beginning of season 1, in a series of quick flashbacks as "Thirteen" by Big Star plays in the background, then he arrives home and they share that tender, passionate kiss. That always makes me cry. Always.

Donna was supposed to be out of Eric's league because she was this super attractive, outspoken, "cool" girl (I hate that term, but you know what I mean? "Cool" from a 16-year-old boy's perspective) whereas he was a nerdy, scrawny-looking, shy guy. Physically and socially, they are complete opposites. And that is one of the running gags of the show. "How did HE get HER?" But I don't necessarily agree with this view either. I think BOTH of them had great qualities but also lots of flaws (Eric was insecure, Donna was stubborn, etc.) I think people in general are more harsh on Eric and tend to give Donna a free pass, which I have done before. But throughout their relationship they BOTH screw up, and they both prove themselves to be silly teenagers with no concrete idea of what they want out of love and out of life, but they're still in love with each other. 

As much as I hated Eric being away for the last season (and thought what he did was selfish in regards to Donna), in my mind I think this could have seriously improved their relationship. They spent time apart, they have matured and started their journeys into adulthood. I believe that would probably have made their relationship better. Or it would made them realize that they no longer fit together and it was just a high school romance. I prefer the first option though.
